pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:96 The card's play button flips to its 'pause' face when the request is issued, before the element echoes `playing`, and no `waiting`/`stalled` listener exists, so loading, buffering and playing all look the same on the card — the request-versus-fact split the transport-contract requires.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:96 The state comes from the request, not the engine echo (TakeCard renders `on={playing === h.id}`). There is no loading or buffering state. The watchdog (line 98) and gen-based supersession (line 86) are present and correct.
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:66 On unmount the cleanup clears the watchdog, removes the listeners, pauses, drops the src and calls load(), so no audio outlives the surface.
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:114 Position is read on demand from the element, the single authority. Nothing stores it in React state.

app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:86 There is one native HTMLAudioElement and no seek or volume affordance, so no capabilities need declaring. The exclusivity claim is made synchronously when the request is issued.
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:53 Playback here is one take at a time, chosen by the user, so there is no blacklist or fallback ladder to design. A failure is reported in words.
app/(studio)/audio/_audio/useTransport.ts:98 One take plays at a time and nothing is composed on a timeline.

pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx:30 The cut and score editors share one clock store that lives outside React and is advanced by a rAF loop; the needle, readout and monitor subscribe through selectors and derive the shown scene from clock time.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx:30 The clock is a mutable store fed by rAF. useClockT selects at each consumer's own cadence (the Readout at Cut.tsx:62 re-renders only when the timecode changes).

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:67 The monitor's scene is a pure function of clock time over the composition, so a seek simply re-derives it. Nothing is chained clip to clip. The sound lanes are not voiced under the clock; this is a silent picture preview.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx:300 The frame loop is cancelled on pause and on unmount. Render.tsx:70 does the same for the poster preview loop.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx:314 The transport drives a virtual clock with no media engine behind it, so there is no transition to await or put a watchdog on. The end is handled (line 297).
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Cut.tsx:123 Take audio plays through the platform's stock controls, with no transport owned by the app. The golden path exempts that case.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Render.tsx:40 Nothing plays continuously from a stream. An undecodable still is reported through an ErrorLine.
